## What you are likely to serve

In England and Wales the rules changed on 1 October 2026. For a standard determinate sentence that is not on the exclusion list, the earliest release point is now **one third**, not halfway. Misconduct in prison can push that later. There is no Parole Board hearing for a normal fixed term, but release at the earliest point is not guaranteed if you pick up adjudications. [[1]](https://insidetime.org/information/sentencing-act-what-the-changes-to-release-dates-mean-for-you/)[[2]](https://www.defence-barrister.co.uk/release-from-custodial-sentences)[[3]](https://www.thetrentonline.com/england-wales-700-prisoners-early-release-sentencing-act/)

On 18 months, one third is **6 months**. Halfway is **9 months**. Every day already spent on remand counts as a day served, so the clock does not start from the sentencing hearing if you were held beforehand.

GBH itself is not on the offence exclusion list. Domestic-abuse cases are not carved out of this scheme either, unless the conviction is for something that is excluded, such as rape or unlawful killing. Section 18 and section 20 both sit outside that list. [[2]](https://www.defence-barrister.co.uk/release-from-custodial-sentences)[[4]](https://womensaid.org.uk/information-support/prisoner-early-release-domestic-abuse/)

Tagging out early on Home Detention Curfew is basically gone for adults. From 2 September 2026 it stopped being routinely available, because the earlier release point replaced it. [[5]](https://prisonreformtrust.org.uk/adviceguide/home-detention-curfew-hdc/)

The prison’s offender management unit calculates the actual date. Your solicitor should be able to tell you the conditional release date once the warrant is processed. Do not rely on a back-of-the-envelope figure if you had a long remand, consecutive terms, or time already served on another matter.

## Which GBH matters

“GBH” is two different offences.

- **Section 20** (wounding or inflicting GBH, no intent to cause really serious harm): maximum 5 years. Guideline range runs from a community order up to about 4½ years. Eighteen months sits inside that range.
- **Section 18** (GBH with intent): maximum life. Typical custodial ranges start around 2–3 years even at the bottom and run much higher. An 18-month term for section 18 would be unusually low.

Domestic context is an aggravating factor. From today, courts also have to say in open court when an offence involved domestic abuse. That finding follows you into prison and probation records. [[6]](https://www.jdspicer.co.uk/site/blog/crime-fraud/sentencing-guidelines-for-GBH)[[7]](https://sentencingcouncil.org.uk/updates/amendments-made-to-sentencing-guidelines-on-5-october-2026-as-a-result-of-the-sentencing-act-2026/)

## After release

The sentence does not end when you walk out. You stay on licence until the 18 months is up. Standard conditions plus, in a case like this, almost always:

- no contact with her, direct or indirect, including through other people or social media
- an exclusion zone around her home, work, or anywhere she is known to be
- a residence requirement and probation appointments
- often a programme requirement

Breach means recall. Contact in breach of a restraining order or non-molestation order is a separate criminal offence, not just a licence issue. Her side may be on the Victim Contact Scheme, because this is a specified violent offence and the sentence is over 12 months. Probation can tell her your release timing. You will not get to manage that.

## If you think the sentence is wrong

Any appeal against sentence normally has to be lodged within **28 days** of the hearing. Speak to the solicitors who had the case this week, not after you have settled into the wing. Grounds are legal (wrong category, wrong credit for plea, manifestly excessive), not “I disagree.”
